method: Independent read-only source review of the three candidate HTML pages. Checked navigation and focus CSS, semantic landmarks and heading levels, table headers and narrow-width overflow CSS. No browser rendering or interaction was performed.

browser_availability.probe: Get-Command chrome, msedge, chromium, chromium-browser -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
browser_availability.result: No executable was returned for these browser command names.

observations: One nav landmark has aria-label Main navigation; links are native anchors and nav links wrap in CSS.
a:focus-visible defines a 3px accent outline for links.
No skip link is present before the repeated navigation.
Heading sequence is h1 DOMASEED, section h2 headings, then FAQ h3 questions; no table is present.
At max-width 700px CSS changes section layout to block and reduces page padding; actual 200% zoom reflow was not measured.
One nav landmark has aria-label Main navigation; links are native anchors and nav flex-wrap is enabled.
a:focus-visible defines a 3px accent outline for links.
No skip link is present before the repeated navigation.
One h1 is followed by section h2 headings. The comparison table has thead, tbody, scope=col column headers and scope=row row headers.
The table is inside .table-wrap with overflow-x:auto; horizontal scrolling and screen magnifier usability were not tested in a browser.
One nav landmark has aria-label Main navigation; links are native anchors and nav flex-wrap is enabled.
a:focus-visible defines a 3px accent outline for links.
No skip link is present before the repeated navigation.
One h1 is followed by h2 section headings. Comparison sheet and further reading use semantic unordered lists; no table is present.
Responsive CSS reduces horizontal padding at max-width 480px; actual narrow viewport and 200% zoom were not measured.

findings.location: All three pages, body > main > nav, before header
findings.impact: Keyboard and switch users must traverse the repeated navigation on each page before reaching page content.
findings.recommendation: Add a first-focusable skip link targeting a main element with a stable id; reveal it on focus and verify keyboard focus visibility.

findings.issue: The wide comparison table uses horizontal scrolling at constrained widths.
findings.impact: At narrow viewport or high zoom, users may need two-dimensional navigation and may lose row/column context; source inspection cannot establish whether it remains usable.
findings.recommendation: Test at 320 CSS px and 200% zoom with keyboard and screen magnification. If scanning is difficult, provide a stacked alternative or otherwise preserve clear row and column context.

limitations: This is source inspection, not a browser accessibility audit or conformance claim.
No actual keyboard focus traversal, screen reader, narrow-screen viewport or 200% zoom test was run.
No online page was changed or published.
